subject: Integrations: rerank pilot — auth, routing, and top_k tuning (post-call)
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@seekedge.com>, Priya Shah <priya@seekedge.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Integrations: rerank pilot — auth, routing, and top_k tuning (post-call)

Thanks for the call this morning — good alignment on scope. Quick recap and concrete asks so we can kick off the pilot:

Recap (short):
- Objective: replace current post-filtering with a learned reranker to improve top results for product search (desktop + mobile).
- Data: you'll provide ~5k labeled queries for initial eval + logs for live sampling.
- Success metrics: NDCG uplift vs current BM25 baseline, improved CTR on top result, and Recall@10 for cold queries.

Open/Action items for SeekEdge (please confirm):
1) SDK + auth: confirm backend stack (we heard Python/FastAPI) and whether you prefer API keys or OIDC client-credentials/KMS integration for long-term SSO.
2) Routing & region: all traffic currently in us-west; do you need multi-region routing / fallback (we support auto-fallback to smaller model family under load)?
3) Structured output: we recommend the reranker return a JSON payload per candidate: {id, score, normalized_score, explain_tokens[]}. Will that integrate with your ranking pipeline?
4) top_k tuning: propose to start with top_k=10 for offline eval and then sweep 5/10/20 during the live A/B. Any constraints on downstream latency when increasing top_k?
5) Eval dataset: please share a small sample (anonymized) and a couple of baseline labels so we can produce NDCG/MRR estimates.

Attached: rerank-integration-spec.md (integration checklist) and proposed-map.xlsx (routing & auth options matrix).

Proposed next steps:
- Tech workshop (30–45m) with your backend engineer + our infra engineer (available Mon/Tue next week).
- We’ll draft an eval rubric and a small PoC plan (timelines, data needs).

If you can reply with the preferred auth approach and upload a 200–500 query sample to the Drive link you created, we’ll prepare the workshop agenda.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0148

Attachments: rerank-integration-spec.md (text), proposed-map.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@seekedge.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya@seekedge.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Integrations: rerank pilot — auth, routing, and top_k tuning (post-call)

Thanks Mina — great recap. Quick answers from our side and a few clarifying questions: 

Stack: Python (FastAPI) + Redis cache; backend runs in AWS us-west-2.
Auth: short-term we can use API keys, but long-term we need KMS-backed keys and preferably OIDC for service-to-service. Our security team will want KMS encrypt-at-rest for any persistent keys.
Routing: we only run in us-west now; fallback to smaller model is fine as long as latency stays within 120ms p50 for the reranked step.
Structured output: returning JSON with id & score is fine; explain_tokens would be nice but not strictly required — depends on payload size. Can the explanation be optional per request?
Top_k: latency constraint: our search pipeline adds ~12ms per candidate after the reranker; so increasing top_k beyond 20 will likely push p95 over acceptable bounds. Start at 10, evaluate at 5/10/20.
Eval data: attaching a 500-row sample (anonymized). I will also invite our backend lead, Kyle Nguyen (kyle@seekedge.ai), to the tech workshop and put the sample in the Drive folder.

One question: does Redwood’s ranking API return raw logits or only normalized scores (0–1)? For our analysis we’d prefer both if possible. Also curious about payload compression for the explainers — any recommendations?

Thanks,
Sam
Head of Product Engineering | SeekEdge
sam.patel@seekedge.com

Attachments: seekedge_sample_queries.csv

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@seekedge.com>, Priya Shah <priya@seekedge.com>, Kyle Nguyen <kyle@seekedge.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Integrations: rerank pilot — auth, routing, and top_k tuning (post-call)

Thanks Sam — appreciate the sample and the specifics. Short answers and a concrete tech plan below.

Auth / Keys:
- Short-term: API keys work for the PoC. We provide scoped keys and usage limits.
- Long-term: OIDC (client credentials) + KMS/HSM integration is supported. We can integrate with AWS KMS to rotate the decryption key for tokens; our engineers will share an example Terraform snippet at the workshop.

SDK / Quickstart (Python):
- We have a small FastAPI-ready client. Quick snippet (Python):

from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="<REDACTED>")
# batch up candidates, call /v1/rank with model=rdr-re1
response = client.rank(model="rdr-re1", query="running shoes", candidates=[{"id":"p123","text":"red running shoe"}])
# response["top_k"] -> list of {id, score, normalized_score, explain}

- Supports async calls, streaming candidate scoring, and batch endpoints to amortize overhead.

Scores / Explanations:
- We can return both raw logits and normalized scores (0-1). For most production flows we recommend sending normalized_score and an optional explain JSON.
- Explain payloads are optional per request (client can set explain=true). For payload size, we recommend returning token-level explanations trimmed to top 5 tokens or a condensed textual rationale. We also support gzip compression on responses.

Routing & Latency:
- Default p50 for the model family is ~65ms for rerank on GPUs with continuous batching; p95 depends on burst load and batch size.
- Recommend client-side circuit-breaker: if observed p95 > 200ms, fall back to a scored heuristic model (we can return a lightweight score).

Top_k tuning & Eval plan:
- Offline: run NDCG@5, NDCG@10, MRR, and Recall@10. Start with top_k=10 for offline and log results for k in {5,10,20}.
- Live: run an A/B for 2 weeks with incremental rollout, monitor CTR on position 1 and query-level win-rate.
- Sample size guidance: for pairwise win-rate with 95% power expect ~200–500 holdout queries depending on effect size — we’ll produce a short power analysis in the eval-rubric.pdf (attached).

Integration payload (recommended):
- return JSON: {"top_k": [{"id":"...","score":-2.34,"norm_score":0.82,"explain":"token:boost"}], "model_version":"rdr-re1-v2","timing_ms":45}

Next steps I’ll take before the workshop:
- Share the eval-rubric.pdf (attached) — includes metric definitions, logging schema, and minimum sample sizes.
- Draft the Terraform snippet for KMS + OIDC and include in the workshop notes.
- Propose Wed 09:00 or Thu 14:00 PT for the 45m technical session.

Rishi — I’ve cc’d you for pricing & commitment discussion. Sam/Kyle — can you confirm Wed/Thu availability and whether you want explanations enabled in the PoC?

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.ai

Attachments: eval-rubric.pdf
